channel.title: Languages on 梦兽编程
channel.description: Recent content in Languages on 梦兽编程

item.title: Rust + AWS Lambda: Secure Credential-Free Access with Workload Credentials
item.description: How Rust Lambdas automatically obtain temporary credentials via IAM roles — from IAM role creation, Rust code implementation to cargo-lambda deployment, a hands-on walkthrough of the AWS Workload Credentials Provider workflow.

item.title: Building AI Agents in Rust — The Tool-Calling Loop Explained
item.description: A deep dive into the core mechanism of AI agents: the tool-calling loop. Through a ~200-line Rust implementation, we break down how models gain the ability to act via tool use, and why the architecture behind Claude Code and GitHub Copilot is the same fundamental loop.

item.title: Rust-Written Lua Compiler Runs Scripts Natively on Bare-Metal Arduino
item.description: TinyLua: a zero-VM Lua native compiler written in Rust. Compiles Lua source directly to AVR/ARM machine code for Arduino bare-metal — no interpreter, no GC, no runtime. Scripting language performance at C level.

item.title: Rust Smart Pointers Complete Guide: Box, Rc, and RefCell Explained with Code Examples
item.description: Master Rust smart pointers: Box, Rc, RefCell, and the powerful Rc<RefCell<T>> combo. Learn heap allocation, reference counting, and interior mutability through vivid analogies. Beginner to intermediate level.

item.title: Go 2026 Survival Guide for Backend Engineers: The Changes That Actually Affect Production
item.description: Go 1.25 and 1.26 bring container-aware GOMAXPROCS, go fix overhaul, Green Tea GC, testing/synctest, and more. A practical breakdown of what backend engineers actually need to know.

item.title: tokio::select! Finally Gets rustfmt Support: A Hands-On Look at better_tokio_select
item.description: The tokio::select! macro has always been a blind spot for rustfmt. better_tokio_select uses match syntax to fix this, so your async Rust code can finally be auto-formatted.

item.title: Why a Pure-Rust HTML-to-PDF Engine Could Be a Bigger Deal Than Most Developers Realize
item.description: Still using headless Chromium for PDF generation? That might change soon. A lightweight Rust library is redefining document rendering boundaries—it runs on the edge, compiles to WASM, and needs no browser.

item.title: Java's Quiet Revolution: How February 2026 Changed Everything You Thought You Knew About the JVM
item.description: February 2026 brings a quiet revolution to the Java ecosystem: JEP 531 lazy constants optimize startup performance, TornadoVM 3.0 brings Java to GPUs, and Chicory enables WebAssembly-JVM interoperability. From Open Liberty security patches to Quarkus integrating Project Leyden, Java is redefining itself for the cloud-native and AI era.

item.title: Rust is Taking Over GPU Programming: 239K Lines Replacing the Entire CUDA Ecosystem
item.description: Oxide Computer released OxiCUDA, a pure Rust implementation of the complete NVIDIA CUDA software stack. 239K lines of safe Rust code, 28 crates, zero C toolchain. This is production-ready code, not a proof of concept.

item.title: Rust's #[must_use]: Making Sure Your Return Values Can't Be Ignored
item.description: Rust #[must_use] attribute explained: put it on structs, functions, or traits to force callers to handle critical return values. Compile-time warnings prevent transactions and payments from being silently dropped.

item.title: Rust 10x Faster Than Spring? I Ran the Benchmarks. The Truth Is More Complicated.
item.description: Behind the benchmark numbers are three competing models: GC pauses, JIT warmup, and AOT compilation. Here's the data-driven breakdown of when to use Rust versus when Quarkus Native Image is the smarter choice.

item.title: Rust 1.94 is Here: Sliding Window Pattern Matching Makes Code Elegant
item.description: Rust 1.94 brings three major updates: sliding windows destructured into named variables, Cargo.toml now supports multi-line syntax, and the Golden Ratio finally joins after 10 years!

item.title: From 1GB to 40MB: How Rust Cracks Memory Management
item.description: Same microservice, same endpoints, but memory usage dropped from 1GB to 40MB after rewriting Node.js to Rust. That's 25x less memory. How does Rust pull this off? Let's talk about ownership.

item.title: Go + sqlc + Postgres: The Zero-ORM Stack Behind Cloudflare's 99.99% Uptime
item.description: Cloudflare runs Go + sqlc + Postgres in production, bypassing GORM's N+1 queries and reflection overhead. 85K vs 42K qps, p99 drops from 3.8ms to 1.2ms. Breaking down the design logic, migration patterns, and when it actually makes sense to switch.

item.title: How Does Kotlin Code Actually Run on iPhone? The KMP Compilation Pipeline Explained
item.description: Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) compiles Kotlin code into native iOS ARM64 machine code through Kotlin/Native and LLVM. This article breaks down the full 7-step compilation pipeline from Kotlin source to LLVM IR, Objective-C bridging, and Swift interop, with performance insights and build optimization tips.

item.title: Just 'Know Python' on Your Resume? Hiring Managers Aren't Buying It in 2026
item.description: The 2026 Python job market has changed: writing scripts isn't enough anymore. This guide breaks down 9 Python skill areas that actually impress interviewers, with a 4-phase learning roadmap and salary benchmarks.

item.title: We Compared 6 Outage Reports Before We Understood What Async Rust Actually Prevents
item.description: CPU was fine, memory was stable, no recent deploys — but error rates hit 3.4%. After comparing 6 outage reports across Node.js, Go, and Java, we finally understood how async systems actually fail, and where Rust+Tokio's compiler draws the line.

item.title: Go 1.26 Shipped Without JSON v2: 18 of 44 Tasks Still Open
item.description: Go 1.26 is out, but JSON v2 remains experimental. With 18 of 44 subtasks still open, unresolved performance regressions, and pending Union type support—this isn't a delay, it's the Go team building a solid foundation for the standard library.

item.title: Don't Underestimate Rust Enums: A Complete Hands-On Guide
item.description: Rust enums are far more than a set of constants. They carry data, drive state machines, replace null, and unify error handling. This guide walks you from basics to recursive enums with real code examples.

item.title: 500 Lines of Rust, 10 Seconds to Train: How Simple Is Building a Neural Network from Scratch?
item.description: Build a spam classifier neural network with Rust and Hugging Face's Candle framework in just 500 lines of code. From tokenizer to embedding to Softmax, every step explained like a cooking recipe. No GPU, no Python, runs on any laptop.

item.title: 4000 Pages Per Second: The Rust PDF Library That's Changing the Game
item.description: oxidize-pdf: A pure-Rust PDF engine with zero C dependencies, a 5MB binary, and performance that leaves Chromium and Java stacks in the dust.

item.title: Brave Browser Rewrites Ad Blocker in Rust, Slashes Memory by 75%
item.description: Brave 1.85 rewrites its ad-blocking engine using Rust and FlatBuffers, reducing memory usage from 60MB to 15MB. Here's how they did it.

item.title: Stop Writing Some(...): The impl Into<Option<T>> Trick in Rust
item.description: Learn how to use Rust's Into Trait with Option to let functions accept both raw values and Option types, eliminating tedious Some() wrapping.

item.title: Rust 1.93 Released: musl Upgrade, Assembly Conditional Compilation, Zero-Copy Suite
item.description: Rust 1.93 is out with all musl targets upgraded to 1.2.5, #[cfg] conditional compilation in assembly, global allocators can now use TLS, and zero-copy APIs stabilized.

item.title: Homebrew Too Slow? Try This Rust Version, 20x Faster
item.description: ZeroBrew is a Rust-based Homebrew alternative that installs packages lightning fast. Let's talk about why it's so fast and how to safely try it out.

item.title: Rust GCC Compiler Backend: Install rustc-codegen-gcc with One Command
item.description: rustc-codegen-gcc is now officially part of rustup nightly components. Linux users can now experience GCC-compiled Rust code with a single command. No more manual compilation, no more environment setup hassles—it's like giving Rust a new engine.

item.title: Rust's Standard Library Now Runs on GPUs: What Did They Actually Do
item.description: VectorWare team made Rust's std library work on GPUs. You can now use println!, read files, and get system time inside GPU kernels. Here's how they pulled it off.

item.title: The Truth About Rust Cold Starts on AWS Lambda: Those Scary Numbers
item.description: A chat with a friend about the cold start performance differences between Rust and Go on AWS Lambda. Why does Rust seem to lose? When should you use which language? The stories hidden behind those monitoring charts.

item.title: Rust Multimedia: A 21-Year-Old Rewriting FFmpeg in Rust—Crazy or Genius?
item.description: A 21-year-old developer, Ajay Kumar, is rewriting FFmpeg from scratch in pure Rust. Why would anyone do this, and what does Rust change for multimedia work?

item.title: Const Generics: This Rust Feature Cut Our Code by 85%
item.description: From 8,347 lines to 1,243 lines — the rebirth of a cryptography library

item.title: Xiao Li Rewrote Go Monolith to Rust Axum, Company Saved $800K+ Yearly, His Salary Hit $2M
item.description: This isn't a story about flexing how fast Rust is. It's about how tech choices translate to real money, and why most rewrite projects can't replicate this result.

item.title: The Rust Async Trap Everyone Steps On Once
item.description: It compiles. It runs. It even passes stress tests... until production catches fire. Let's talk about that classic async Rust pitfall everyone hits.

item.title: Rust Design Patterns: 3 Best Practices Senior Backend Engineers Always Use
item.description: Discover the Rust design patterns senior engineers swear by: Newtype pattern prevents invalid states, ownership design reflects system boundaries, enum error handling makes failures predictable. Master these Rust best practices to build rock-solid backend code and say goodbye to midnight incidents.

item.title: I Rewrote Our Python Data Pipeline in Rust: 3 Hours to 4 Minutes, 40x Faster
item.description: A real-world case study of rewriting a Python data pipeline with Rust + DuckDB. From 3-hour daily ETL jobs to 4-minute runs, memory usage dropped from 12GB to 600MB, and server costs cut by two-thirds.

item.title: Rust Compiler Pipeline Refactor: 35% Faster Build Times, But There's a Catch
item.description: Our team's CI dropped from 42 minutes to 27 minutes just by upgrading the Rust compiler. This journey taught us one thing: performance optimization rewards those who measure, punishes those who guess.

item.title: 10x Performance Boost Secret: 99% Don't Know These Go Concurrent GC Tricks
item.description: Production latency dropped from 500ms to 50ms! Deep dive into Go's tri-color marking algorithm, write barriers, and GOGC tuning. Say goodbye to lag forever.

item.title: Rust Lifetimes Scare Away 90% of Programmers? One Library Analogy Gets You There in Seconds
item.description: Compiler errors got you running? Relax. Rust lifetimes aren't scary monsters—they're invisible guardians ensuring your code never crashes. This 5-minute guide beats the official docs.

item.title: Rust Performance Pitfalls: When Rust Runs Slower Than Python
item.description: Rust performance optimization in practice: I watched my Rust rewrite get crushed by Python. The problem was data structure choice.

item.title: Python Finally Got Fast: JIT Compiler Makes Code Performance Take Off
item.description: Python 3.15 introduces a native JIT compiler that delivers 20% performance improvements without changing a single line of code. Here's how to enable this experimental feature.

item.title: From 800ms to 90ms: How Rust Rayon Saved My Multithreading Nightmare
item.description: A real Rust concurrency case study: replacing manual threads with Rayon's work-stealing scheduler and getting a 9x speedup.

item.title: io_uring Guide: Building High-Performance Servers with Rust and Async IO
item.description: A friendly deep-dive into Linux io_uring async IO technology, learn how to build high-performance servers with Rust and escape syscall bottlenecks

item.title: Rust mmap Memory-Mapped I/O: Why Reading Files Can Be as Fast as Accessing Memory
item.description: A plain-English guide to Rust mmap memory-mapped I/O. Why is it 5-10x faster than traditional Rust file reading? How does zero-copy achieve Rust performance optimization? This memmap2 hands-on tutorial uses real-life analogies to help you understand this seemingly mysterious low-level technology.

item.title: Pop!_OS 24.04 is Here: The World's First Rust-Built Desktop Environment
item.description: System76 releases Pop!_OS 24.04 and COSMIC desktop environment - the first production-grade desktop environment written entirely in Rust, challenging 20 years of GTK/Qt dominance. In-depth review: performance, customization, and tiling window management

item.title: Is the Electron Era Ending? Rust GPUI Lets You Stop Compromising on Cross‑Platform
item.description: Electron made desktop cross‑platform easy; Rust GPUI makes it feel native fast. This beginner‑friendly briefing explains the core idea, the minimal runnable path, and a humane migration plan.

item.title: I Told Old Zhang His Rust Service Might Be 10x Slower - He Almost Spit Coffee in My Face
item.description: Rust service suddenly 10x slower? The problem might be hiding in Serde macros. This article walks through a real story to help you identify and fix performance issues caused by Serde serialization.

item.title: I Fired My Entire Node.js Stack — Rust Rebuilt It in 3 Weeks (The Ugly Truth)
item.description: API latency dropped from 850ms to 8ms, monthly costs from $12,000 to $900. Sounds great? The price was three months of hell and a team on the verge of collapse. This is a real backend migration story.

item.title: I Thought Rust Was Over-Engineering—Until I Saw the Production Logs
item.description: A 2 AM production incident made me rethink Rust. From 8 crashes per hour to zero crashes—this isn't about language wars, it's about trust.
